title: The End ...?
subtitle: "Things are rarely as they appear at the scene of a crime."

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof ... woof!

items.speaker: Wendy
items.text: Woof woof!

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof woof ... woof woof!

items.speaker: Police Dog
items.text: Woof woof woof!

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof woof woof woof!
Pickles's struggling and crying for help are swallowed by the festive realm. The hero puppy is surrounded by the excited crowd.
Together with the Rimet Cup.
Charlton wakes up at this very moment. He awkwardly but happily accepts everything.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: Hello, sir. Are you the owner of this hero puppy?

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Not exactly. I'm his friend, best friend.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: Um ... Would you mind telling us how you raised such a brilliant dog?

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: I guess people will care about the puppy's daily life after the article's published.

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Well, I often enjoy the symphony with him. Sometimes we'll discuss profound philosophical issues together.

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Yes. We have quite an extensive collection of books at home, for example, Meditationes de Prima Philosophia, The Republic, Rhetoric to Alexander ...

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: That's an informative first-hand material.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: Thanks for your cooperation, Mr. Owner.

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: It's been a pleasure to be interviewed by you. Pickles, too.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: That's beautiful. We may have further and more detailed interviews that need your cooperation. A constant stream of interviews, film shoots, and friendly matches with the England national football team will follow.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: I'm sure the team would also like to thank the hero who guarded the cup in person.

items.speaker: Journalist
items.text: The puppy's heroic act may even be highly appealing to film investors.

items.speaker: Charlton
items.text: Really?!

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woooof woooof.

items.speaker: Pickles
items.text: Woof …
People are not able to share happiness or divide sorrow, even if they stand in the same exhibition hall.
On the other side of the hall, someone else is crying.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Wandering is my destiny.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: After an unprecedented and unexpected soap bubble surprise party ...

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: None of them left anything improvised about Utopia!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Not even one of them mentioning my contribution! All the people ignored a pioneer who created a new era!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: A monumental event was shamefully compared to a puppy!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Ahh! Art is dead.
That's one of the stories I've come across, readers of UTTU.
It's dramatic—full of misunderstandings, lovely animals, and terrifying intrigues, again providing us with a ludicrous ending.
I'm glad to have the great honor to share this with you.
Wherever you are, whatever you've been ... I hope this story will bring you a moment of joy.
And I am also sincerely looking forward to ... your stories.
THE END

The Sixth Etiquette
Sotheby's Dream
A cotton swab dipped in iodine is gently pressed against Sotheby's wound.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Ooh, ouch ...
Miss, please bear with me for a moment. It'll be over soon.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh! N-No, I didn't mean it! It doesn't hurt. Keep going.
Moonlight streams through the floor-length windows and into the quiet room.
The gentle sound of the piano fills the air.
I admit music can distract from and alleviate pain, but even the most moving melody loses its charm when played repeatedly. Miss, perhaps you should try a different piece.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: But I like playing this one.
In that case, you need to learn a new piece. I assure you, you'll enjoy playing something new.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Ouch!
I do apologize, Ms. Sotheby. Does the potion sting?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Mr. Karson ...

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: Yes, my lady?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: If this tiny wound hurts this much, what does it feel like to die?

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: Hmm. That's a good question, and you asked the right person.

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: Are you afraid of death?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: I-I wasn't afraid before. It was just a nightmare, a darkness or long sleep.

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: And now?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Now ...

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: I'm a little scared.

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: Why?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Because it'll take my friends away.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Like they'll fall asleep and never wake up.

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: Alright, switch hands.
Sotheby extends her other hand, and Mr. Karson gently applies the cotton swab to the wound on it.

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: Ultimately, you're afraid of loneliness.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: I'm not afraid of loneliness. Sotheby is not afraid of loneliness.

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: It's quite alright, my lady. No one wants to be lonely.

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: But loneliness is not a monster; it's not enough to overwhelm a person.

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: There are many people in this world who have done wrong in their lives, and oftentimes they don't even know why they do it.

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: Ultimately, it's because they're afraid of being lonely.

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: But the fact is, loneliness isn't that scary.

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: Just as all monsters have an Achilles' heel, loneliness has its remedy.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: What is it?

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: I think you may already know the answer, my lady.
He puts down the cotton swab and carefully inspects Sotheby's wounds.

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: I'm afraid I have to go now.

items.speaker: Mr. Karson
items.text: I'll come and see you next time. I'm sure that by then, you'll be an even more trustworthy young lady.
Sotheby's Room

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Hmm ... huh ... did I fall asleep ...?
A light knock raps on the door before it creaks open.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Can I come in?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Hmm? Oh, it's you! Of course!
The little Scout slowly shuffles in.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Ms. Sotheby, how's that potion coming along?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh! The potion! Yes, it's all finished. They're in these test tubes over here.
Sotheby proudly raises her head as she shows her friend her masterpiece.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: I already gave Ms. Cristallo a little bit. Once she wakes up, she can drink some more, and it'll work even better!
Eagle stands by the door, wanting to come closer but feeling too timid to do so.
Sotheby strides over to Eagle, takes her hand, and leads her to the experimentation table. She taps the test tubes.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Listen. Don't they make a pretty sound?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: "Ding ding dang dong," "boo bop du dop," such bright melodies!
Eagle tentatively reaches out a finger and, like Sotheby, gently taps the test tubes.
They sway like wind chimes, producing a series of crisp sounds.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Hehe, do you like it? I love doing this on a quiet night. It's so much fun!

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Yeah, I like it. It's interesting.
She smiles shyly, but behind her eyes, it's clear to see that she has something to say.
Sotheby looks at Eagle, places the test tube aside, and sits back on the bed, swinging her legs.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Well, Ms. Eagle, I-I still want to play with her.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: I want to be with my friends forever and ever.
She lowers her eyes.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: No! No—I ...
She plays with her fingers anxiously, not knowing what to say.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I, I'm actually here to apologize.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: After you left, I kept thinking about what I said to you before.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I ... you see ... I ...

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I shouldn't have said those things to you—not just about hoping you wouldn't play with her, but, many, many other things, too.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I don't even know why I said it.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Maybe it was because I also want to be friends with you, but I don't know how.
Sotheby opens a small tin box that she pulled from the cabinet.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Try this.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: When you described the Pop-a-Rock Rainbow Candy to me before, I thought, wouldn't it be nice if there was a candy that, after eating it, you could see a rainbow?
Sotheby puts one in her mouth as well, and the two of them chew together.
They chew and chew.
And chew and chew some more.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: They're a bit tough, aren't they?
The two look at each other. Sotheby is wincing, her hand on her aching jaw.
They giggle.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Hey, I see it. There's a rainbow!
Eagle points to the ceiling.
There's nothing there.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: One, two, three ... seven, just like Heimdall said, seven colors!
The two of them tilt their heads back, grinning at the empty ceiling.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Look! It's Typhon!

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: He's walking on the rainbow bridge. Hey! Where's he going?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Someone's stopping him. Who is that?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: That's Heimdall, the great hero who guards the rainbow bridge. He's giving Typhon directions!

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Where's Typhon going?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: He's going to battle with Jupiter and his army!

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Who's Jupiter?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh, he's a really bad man. His minions are always giving Typhon trouble. They've even come to bother me, but I managed to drive them off!

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Wow—that's amazing!

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I hereby present you, Lady Sotheby, Captain of Typhon's army and leader in the victorious battle against Jupiter's army, with this first-class medal of honor.
The little Scout wobbles as she sits up, unpins the badge from her chest, and solemnly pins it to Sotheby's dress.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: It is my honor, Commander!
Sotheby wobbles as she sits up and gives Eagle a less-than-perfect salute.
Eagle adjusts Sotheby's hand to the correct salute position, then lies back down.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Hehe! Hahaha!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Hahaha!
The two laugh together.
The night is still long.

The Lady's Code of Conduct: Revised Edition

The Hall in the Suitcase

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The results of Cristallo's examination are in. A coagulation dysfunction caused temporary asphyxiation, which led to her fainting. No plant toxins have been found in her body.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So the popcorn wasn't toxic after all.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We shouldn't have worried so much. She meticulously measured the herbal ingredients, ensuring they would cause no harm to humans.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If there is any effect at all, it's probably just a slight, pleasant hallucination.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There's no denying that she's skilled in managing toxins.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Dale cow tongue isn't a part of a fictional creature, but an arcane herb known as "dyed pearl grass." It's used in basic potions for healing and good luck.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The hoof of the four-legged beast is just a horse's hoof, and Jamaican pepper is also known as "allspice."

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Finally, an Immortal Flower is actually a naturally growing arcane plant called "thousand-spike crop." It's used in some unusual rituals.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She has her own understanding of things, but that doesn't mean the things she mentions don't exist.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Although it won't cure Cristallo's condition, the potion will make her much more comfortable, and she won't faint anymore.
As they speak, a little head peeks out from the wall.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Psst—Ms. Vertin, Ms. Sonetto, come over here.
The little Scout presses her finger to her lips.
With deliberately lowered voices, the children seem to be preparing something—either a prank or a surprise.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What's the matter, Eagle?
A large feathered hat also peeks out from the wall. Their two little heads are stacked one on top of the other. They both frown, their eyes bright and their expressions serious.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Shh! Come here—and turn the lights off.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Walk softly, hurry up!
It feels like she had been in the dark for an eternity.
As consciousness returns to her body, the pale girl slowly sits up, her hand on her forehead.
The emptiness of the room makes her shudder. Before she slept, she was in the middle of the chaos, but now that she's woken up, she's alone again.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Uh ...

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Where am I?

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Oh, this is my room.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: I'm in my room.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: It's so quiet. Nothing like my dream.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: *shiver* It's a bit cold. Is the window open?

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Did someone come in?

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Sotheby, that's right. I remember now.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: She was talking to me, but I couldn't hear her. Then, I can't remember a thing.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Hah.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Seems like I fainted again.
She lowers her head and sighs softly.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: It's so quiet.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: At night, when everyone else is asleep, I'm awake.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: And when everyone else is awake, I'm asleep.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Hmm, maybe I scared her. Should I apologize?

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: "Sorry, I didn't hear what you said," "Sorry for suddenly fainting" ...?

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: It's not like I haven't tried that before. Apologies don't work.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Everyone leaves eventually, and I'll be alone once again.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: You scared her. She won't want to spend time with you anymore.
She sits in familiar silence.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Alright, now let me see if I can close this window.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: *huff, huff* ...
She struggles to prop herself up. As she turns, looking down at her feet dangling off the end of the bed, she notices something.
A small black creature has popped its head out from under the bed.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Ah! What is that?!
It climbs onto the bed, an apologetic look on its face. It grabs her hand in a nervous attempt to comfort her.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Who are ...?

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Are you Typhon?
The little black creature nods excitedly, points to the window, and hops over to close it.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Thank you, Typhon. Did Sotheby send you?
Typhon nods.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Where is she? Does she not want to see me?
Typhon shakes its head frantically.
It points outside the room.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Is she out there?
Typhon doesn't reply. It jumps down from the windowsill and hurries back to Cristallo's bedside, nearly stepping on its own tail on the way.
Taking a deep breath, Typhon begins to grow larger.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: What are you doing? Hey!
It doesn't respond, only growing larger and larger.
Soon, it is so large that its inflated body starts to push Cristallo's bed toward the door.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Where are you taking me?

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Typhon?

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: I-I've never left my room! Just give me a moment to prepare!

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Hey! Typhon, don't scare me! Everyone's asleep! We shouldn't disturb ...

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Don't!
The little black creature continues to manically push Cristallo's bed all the way down the hallway. She has to cling to its sides to balance herself.
The door bursts open.
There is a flash of white light, followed by a sudden, brief dizziness.
Then, above her head, comes the continuous sound of popping. They're not loud, like an explosion, but gentle and fragrant, like a flower bursting open.
*pop* *pop* *pop* The air is quickly filled with a sweet aroma.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Ms. Cristallo!

items.speaker: Everyone
items.text: Cristallo!
The pale girl opens her eyes.

items.speaker: Twins Sleep
items.text: Ms. Cristallo! Come and try some! Come and try some!

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Th-This is ...?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Popping Candy Popcorn!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: I made it with real corn this time!

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Corn?! Did you find a cornfield?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sotheby got some corn seeds from outside the suitcase, so we allocated a piece of land in the Wilderness to grow them on.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We used a growth potion to hasten the growing process.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: You should also thank Ms. Eagle! She came up with the brilliant idea of adding pepper candy to the popcorn—it's even more delicious now!

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Pfft ... *cough* *cough* *cough*
The little Scout blushes as she offers Cristallo a handshake.
Cristallo smiles and takes her hand.
Their hands shake firmly.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Experiment number fifty-three is successful!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: You can draw a smiley face on the sticky note now, Ms. Cristallo!
The popcorn is falling like flower petals.

items.speaker: Twins Sleep
items.text: Lisa has grabbed a lot! Louise has grabbed a lot!

items.speaker: Ms. Moissan
items.text: The blue ones taste like a stream.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: The pink ones are the best! They're like flowers! Wait, no—the green ones are my favorite!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: This APPLe prefers the red ones. They conjure up the image of parchment and a crackling fire, something you'd want to revisit on a winter night with the thrilling works of Christopher Marlowe.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, may I ...?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hmm. Try this one. You'll love it.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: This snack is like nothing I've ever tasted! You can definitely tell it wasn't made in any ordinary factory!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Really?! That's great!
Sotheby, a sparkle in her eyes, raises her head and shouts with joy.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Sotheby is so, so happy!
The feathers on her hat bob happily as she makes her way around the group.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Ms. Cristallo, you simply must try this!
She hands over a piece of golden popcorn.
Cristallo takes it and puts it in her mouth.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Hmm, this is popcorn.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Yes, this is popcorn.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: Popping Candy Popcorn.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Yes, Popping Candy Popcorn.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: It's sweet.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Cristallo
items.text: It's sweet.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Well, well, it seems our story has come to an end. But this is just one of many stories of our little lady making new friends.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: It seems that she is becoming a true lady, isn't she?

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Yes. A very, very good lady indeed.
THE END
Coins, Balloons, and Ribbons
ONiON's show isn't quite over yet.
Thankfully, the water level hasn't risen for quite some time.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Hold on, everyone! We're almost there!
A small boat bears its passengers gently toward the heart of the lake.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Mr. X, your X-301 seems to be sinking by the second.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Don't worry, Ms. Sotheby. This vessel is equipped with special sponges capable of absorbing an unusually high volume of water. By the time we've sunk to the bottom, this thing should've already absorbed at least 85% of the spring water.

items.speaker: X
items.text: That'll be enough to ensure we don't drown.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I hope this doesn't take too long—there's only an hour and fifteen minutes left of the workday.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Fingers crossed!
As the boat continues to drift, the vast waves can no longer conceal a certain petite figure.
Two other figures emerge.
The two figures from the start of ONiON's tale.

items.speaker: Balloon Party
items.text: I kept thinking about the party—thinking and thinking—but I kept thinking that my thinking was wrong. Like something was missing.

items.speaker: Balloon Party
items.text: Now I know what it was! We need water! A big water wave for the party! And you're the best water wave maker I've ever seen! The very best!
She takes La Source's hand, earnestly passing her a balloon.

items.speaker: La Source
items.text: M-Me? I'm the best?

items.speaker: Balloon Party
items.text: Would you like to help us throw a perfect party? I mean, we need more candy and streamers, and balloons, of course!

items.speaker: Balloon Party
items.text: Oh, and more waves! Big ones!

items.speaker: Baby Blue
items.text: We could make that "dragon" a little smaller so he can wear a garland!

items.speaker: La Source
items.text: You ... you'd like me to join you?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Ms. La Source!
The sponge boat has finally reached its destination.
The lake water has already reduced significantly.
A crowd gathers around La Source. For her, this is quite an unusual honor.

items.speaker: La Source
items.text: Ah! Are you here to make a wish?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Actually, we've come to—
He presents his meticulously drafted letter of protest.
La Source doesn't even glance at it. She just shakes her head solemnly.

items.speaker: La Source
items.text: Sorry, I don't have time to help you now!

items.speaker: La Source
items.text: I've accepted an invitation from Baby Blue and Balloon Party! We're going to have the most spectacular, grandest party ever—with big water waves, too!
The group looks on in surprise.

items.speaker: La Source
items.text: Of course, if you'd like to join ...
She starts to think again.

items.speaker: La Source
items.text: Hmm, it's not really asking for something for nothing, so I can agree to that.
X chuckles.

items.speaker: X
items.text: So, you're saying that you have to pull all the spring water you used for wishes back into your pot in order to have your party?

items.speaker: La Source
items.text: Exactly! You didn't think you'd get something for nothing forever, did you?!
She clings to the pot, eyeing X warily.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Ooh-ooh! I'd like to come, please!

items.speaker: Balloon Party
items.text: Certainly, Ms. Sotheby.
They dash off together, four bouncing balloons following in their wake.
Obviously, they have more important things to attend to.
The rest stand there, stunned.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Well, I suppose that's that.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: Looks like I'll be able to clock out on time.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: But I have to say, we really must set up emergency plans and compensation for work stoppages in case something like this happens again.
He opens his umbrella as he works to clear away the mist. Meanwhile, ONiON starts recording again.

items.speaker: X
items.text: It seems you've got yourself some exciting new material, Ms. ONiON. Congratulations.
He nods and makes his way.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Absolutely!

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: I'm planning to showcase another fantastic episode with an in-depth interview and analysis of the central figure! Well, the footage is ready. It just needs some final touches.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: This'll be one for the ages!
She excitedly fiddles with the camera equipment beside her, oblivious to the fact that X is long gone.
The old video player rewinds slowly.
*click*

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen. Brace yourselves, for you are about to witness—

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: The "Getting to Know You" episode of our Spring Elfin Special!

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: This segment's material was captured purely by accident. Nevertheless, I've decided to use it to conclude our story.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: But trust me, this wasn't just a spur-of-the-moment decision—oop!

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Shh, let's keep our voices down.
Not far from the lakeside, Balloon Party, Baby Blue, and ONiON sit on the ground.
The camera, its red light flashing, tilts toward the grass, revealing a figure hidden within.
The child clutching the pot is repeating the same gesture.

items.speaker: La Source
items.text: I-I am the Spring Elfin, La Source!

items.speaker: La Source
items.text: Delighted to m-meet you!

items.speaker: La Source
items.text: Trust me, I can fulfill your wishes! Lots and lots of wishes!

items.speaker: La Source
items.text: If you're willing to be friends with me.
*click*
The last of the mist is drawn into Oliver Fog's umbrella, and he closes it up with a flourish.
*click*
A renewed calm is brought to the suitcase.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: *sigh* An elfin's mood is more unpredictable than the policies of the London authorities.

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: And wasn't I just as naive as any common voter when I made my wish to her?

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I suppose, in the end, we can only depend on ourselves and the friends we hold dear.
He shakes his head in resignation.

items.speaker: ONiON
items.text: Ah, Mr. Fog, I'm glad you're still here. I'm cooking up a new exclusive interview, and I'd love to have you take part!

items.speaker: Oliver Fog
items.text: I'm off duty.
And just like that, the flood is dealt with.
John Titor has yet to grasp the trouble that her wish put everyone through.
She simply puts on her earmuffs and retreats into a world of hexadecimal codes.
Perhaps it's best she stays this way—at least until the greatest party ever conceived has been put on.
THE END
Interview of the "New Humans"

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: ... No doubt. This is a failure. A complete humiliation!

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: The shameless thief stole the exhibit, and sent it back in a package, as if our security was invisible!

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: But this is not a failure of Guidance on Security ... but a failure of us, of our security officers.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Guidance on Security gives us perfect strategies, but the securiy officers were sleepy and negligent ...

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: When the London Police entered the exhibition hall, they were all sound asleep!

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: New Humans shall not allow this to happen again!

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: We promise that human security officer is to be phased out from today, and something more rational, more efficient, and more rigorous is to be introduced—security robots!

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: Over the next three to five years, we are devoted to developing new types, so that human security officers are completely replaced.

items.speaker: Iverson
items.text: We will lead by example and transform the security industry into a future-oriented, science-based, civilised and rational industry!
Melania puts down the magazine, astonished.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: There are flaws in the Guidance, and their response was to fire everyone?

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: Seems Mr. Iverson has completely ignored the Guidance on Security with comments enclosed in my letter ... I pulled two all-nighters for this!

items.speaker: Ms. Acey
items.text: I've warned you. You should finish Prof. Claire's essay first.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text:
And there's not even a word about Ramirez retrieving the Mainedonty.
A lot of journalists were there to interview me ...

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Iverson has way better connections than ours, after all.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: A Ramirez retriving collection's report, at this time? The New Humans are suffering, they won't let it be reported.
Melania stands up, alerted.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: Fiennes ... No. Mr. Sean the Great Thief.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text:
Call me Fiennes like the old days.
I am nothing special.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: You're being modest.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: You are the only international thief of the 20th century who has stolen in London and Paris at the same time.

Her voice sounds cold as the winter Thames.
Obviously, there is no way this conversation can be that kind of awkward small talk they used to have.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: In my defence, I have never committed such a shocking crime.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Just two guards lost the exhibits on the same day, and they used me as an excuse.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: ... What?
She frowns. It's not easy to tell if it's just another lie of "Sean".

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Use your brain, Melania. How would this ever make sense?

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: If my arcane skill is that marvellous, why am I still just a thief?

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Some security guards make up those stories of international thieves to cover their malpractice.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Their imagination can evenly match those of thieves in order not to lose their jobs.
Noticing her being nervous, the Great Thief gives her a smile.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Relax. Well, to be fair, the Mainedonty you have stolen is also a counterfeit.
This is not something she can let go of.
Her jaw drops, but maybe too late.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: Wh-What?

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: My arcane skill is to touch something and make a copy of it. Like what you just heard, it only works on one object once.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: I had copied countless fake antiques with my arcane skill, but at the same time, they would have my arcane mark.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: As their price gets higher and higher, I'm afraid someone will find out that they're all counterfeits. So I decided to steal my copies.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Nothing could stop me back to the days I was in the auctions, exhibitions and museums. I quite enjoyed being unstoppable.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Until your father showed up—My plans fell flat in front of him.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: I thought and thought but still couldn't figure out how he predicted my plan.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: So I applied for Ramirez Security, but only to find that ... your father had no plan, no plan at all!

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: I was the one with a plan in the whole little company!
He lets out a long sigh, a sigh for mourning the time he wasted on his former rival.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: I worked as a security officer for 5 years with full passion.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text:
During that time, I formed an ultimate larceny plan, with all I had learnt from Ramirez.
This was going to be a great thievery that even your father couldn't stop.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: But before I can perform this plan, your father committed suicide. I was disappointed, and upset.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: However, I do know that he considered you as his successor ...

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: ... So, is that a revenge?

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: You asked me to take over the company, and then you stole the exhibits from me, putting an end to Ramirez that almost closed down.

Fiennes opens his mouth as if trying to defend himself.
But before he can say anything, Melania has already grabbed her notebook from the shoulder bag and turned to a certain page.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: Now it makes sense...!

items.speaker: Melania
items.text:
I didn't figure out how you stole the Mainedonty before ...
I thought I had an unconscious bias as the question was set by myself, until I heard about your arcane skill!

items.speaker: Melania
items.text:
You made a copy of Ms. Acey that night, right?
You copied my arcane skill! Then you swapped the exhibit like I did!

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Yes. I trade the Mainedonty with an ice cube in my coffee. After it melts, there was no trace of exchange.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Usually, I can't imitate other arcanist's incantation. But I've worked hard for five years, and the effort paid off—I learnt how to do it once.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: I ought to thank you for that too, Melania, for demonstrating it in front of me.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: Oh my ... the answer is so simple!
She drops into a chair, supporting her forehead with one hand.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text:
So you must have read my plan for The Football Match in the office.
I wrote it all down, and arranged the references alphabetically. Right there on the table!

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: But you still came to the roof. I don't understand ...
He shakes his head, interrupts the young girl's speech with a bitter smile on his face.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: You're like your father, Melania.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: Me ... Like him? That's not possible.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: He always said that the job of a security officer is to ensure the safety of the client's property. Nothing matters except that. His world is nothing but the challenge of attack and defence.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: You, however, after knowing the inside story of the security field and antique trade, you still focus on your "test questions."

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: No. I'm just used to answering questions ...

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Most importantly, you all see this as a self-challange.
Fiennes is caught up in his memory.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Your father was a real artist. Everything became dull after he died.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: I have to say, at first it was an act of revenge on Ramirez ... but I changed my mind.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text:
Melania, you are smart, inquisitive and detail-oriented. You will not miss any chance.
These are valuable qualities, and that's why I went to the patio and met you.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Would you fancy being a thief?

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: You are talented.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: Mr. Fiennes, I have no interest in illegally possessing others' belongings!
Melania blushes. Apparently, an offer of crime is not something she had ever expected.
Fiennes shrugs. Apparently, this offer is just impromptu.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Well, keep leading Ramirez is not a bad choice. You are an elite planner.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: ... No. I'm neither a good question maker nor a business leader.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Thinking from the aspect of a thief is not a common way.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Your father always said, "respect your opponent, and they'll respect you." For that alone, he trumped countless Iversons.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: ... But it's unfair.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text:
Father respected his opponents but was seen as an accomplice.
Both Ramirez and New Humans had lost their exhibits before. When we were seen as a humiliation to the industry, and Father was driven to commit suicide ... What for New Humans?

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: No one ever pointed out the flaws in Guidance on Security ...! Everyone was convinced of his statements. They were drawn to the bumbling robots, while as security officer an ambulance would have been better.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: People are short-sighted, that's not new. They can only see the result.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text:
It doesn't matter whether Guidance on Security is flawless or not. It matters whether people believe it is.
If so, even when something goes wrong, Iverson can blame those idiots instead of the Guidance.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: But it's not the truth!

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: It's the truth in people's eyes.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text:
They are the ones manipulating public opinions.
One success cannot save the credibility of Ramirez. One theft cannot shake the position of the New Humans.
Once again, she grabs the handle of the bag tighter.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: Then I'll prove it to them ...!

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: I'll point out the flaws in Guidance on Security, and I will show the flaws to everyone ... in the same way I did this time!

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: If it happens only once, it may be ignored. But what if it happens twice, three times, and ten?

items.speaker: Melania
items.text:
No security style is better or worse than another, but truth and justice must be manifested. 
The Guidance on Security is not the principles written once and for all ... I must bring it to light ...!
This is an answer beyond Fiennes's imagination.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Is that your choice?

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Then what would you be? The one who keeps writing the legend of Ramirez, or the one who rewrites it?

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: No, Mr Fiennes ...

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: I'm just a student.
The Great Thief looks into the young student's eyes.
The bell at the bar ends this silent competition.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text:
Unfortunately, it's time for me to head to the wharf.
By the way, I used your arcane skill to switch your recording tape. Don't even think about catching me, Melania.
Melania opens her bag in a hurry ....
And sadly finds that he is not lying. She immediately drops her shoulder.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: That's not fair, Mr. Sean. I bought it with my scholarship...

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: You turned down my offer, so don't expect me to teach you any lessons.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: One last thing.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: Arcanists will leave an arcane mark on their works. Proud as your father was, he has no reason not to.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: I have nothing to do with the Rimet Cup case, but I suggest you not underestimate the "imagination of a security officer."
She hops up, shocked.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: Wait. Are you suggesting that there's something else about my Father's case?

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: I just want to see the legend continue.

items.speaker: Fiennes
items.text: It should be tired as your father's daughter, am I right, Melania?
He waved at her elegantly. The next second, he disappeared into the crowd.
Sean the Great Thief has completed his revenge.

items.speaker: Ms. Acey
items.text: He is strange.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: Yes. But free ...
Melania takes a deep breath.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: Ms. Acey, I know what to do.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text:
I can't be like Father or Sean ... and I don't need to.
But I can try to understand them.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text:
One day, I will be back and set my own questions. But before that, I need practice, practice, and practice. 
Until the day when I figure out everything.

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: Could you help me?
The shoulder bag gives her student a playful nibble.

items.speaker: Ms. Acey
items.text: Anytime, Melania.
Weeks later, Ramirez Security Company announces its dissolution.
Meanwhile, an advance notice signed "The Great Thief Acey" was sent to many famous newpapers.
Dear editorial board of Guidance on Security:
Congratulations on the publication.
In the past five years, you've been travelling together with us in the world of imagination.
And now, you are trying to use a guide full of flaws to solve all problems once and for all.
Security, however, shall be art. It requires courage, prudence, creativity and infinite passion.
You respect us no more, so we will respond in the same way.
5 p.m., Sunday, I shall arrive and claim the Light Cross in Naval Museum.
Good luck setting up a perfect security arrangement according to the Guidance.

Sincerely, 
The Great Thief Acey

items.text: Ms. Acey, if Father knew what I was going to do, would he still be proud of me?

items.speaker: Ms. Acey
items.text: I think he would say, "Ace!"

items.speaker: Melania
items.text: I bet he would.
The young thief shoots the hook gun and jumps towards the building.
In the exhibition hall full of miracles and legacies, countless shiny "test questions" await her challenge.

THE END
The Young Investigator
Marcus is like a book swept out to sea, floating directionless through the dead of night.
Familiar pages flash rapidly through her mind.
Echoes of the past ringing yet again in the present.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I remember now ... I wanted to make a choice of my own ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: So I joined the Foundation. I learned of the "Storm." I bade farewell to my era ... and my old dream ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: A choice of my own ... But did I really make one at all?
A sudden agony almost tears the entire book apart.
The spine of the book trembles as it struggles to turn a new page.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Yes, I made my choice. Now see where it's led me. I've ruined everything.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Lady Isolde held a grand exhibition where she made that speech ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I wish for the arcanists to unite ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: And establish an independent kingdom of freedom, free from repression and oppression!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It's all my fault ... If only I hadn't violated the confidentiality agreement, she wouldn't have made that dangerous speech.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: What I did not only failed to help the arcanists, but worse still it intensified the divide between us and humans.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Lady Isolde—and many other innocent arcanists deceived by Manus Vindictae—shouldn't have fallen into such a predicament ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Political assassinations, ethnic conflicts, and civil turmoil have erupted all over the world ... History has been altered; the "Storm" was formed.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I shouldn't have—I should never have called out to Madam Hofmann that day ... I should have stayed on the Flannan Isles!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Madam Hofmann?
Then comes a clearer, more suffocating page.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: No! Madam Hofmann!!!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: *coughs weakly* Don't cry, Marcus. I know what I'm doing.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The future ... is yours.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: No!
This page seems agonizingly long.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: What have I really achieved?
Images bristling with pain and regret ruthlessly intertwine in Marcus's frantic thoughts.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Back on the island, I couldn't even stop my friends from fighting. How could I have thought I would be the one to change humanity's discrimination towards arcanists ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: After I made just that one choice, to join the Foundation, every choice afterward only seemed to magnify the number of people I hurt, even Madam Hofmann ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I never once managed to live up to my aspiration ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: C-Could it be that I ...
The cold abyss stretches out before her. Reality, naked of any illusions.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I've never left the Flannan Isles.
The active cells within her body finally find an outlet amidst the surging pain.
A strange scent invades the air, blurring Marcus's vision.

items.speaker: "Donald"
items.text: M-Ms. Marcus, how did you end up here?

items.speaker: "James"
items.text: Oh, poor lassie, you look miserable ... What sort of trouble have you been in?

items.speaker: "Thomas"
items.text: Dinnae worry, mate. We've always been here for you, always ready to lend you a hand!
The phantoms, as ever before, gather around her with great enthusiasm.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: James ... Donald ... Thomas ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I …
Her long-suppressed emotions finally breach their confines, finding a soothing haven on the windless island.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Aren't you disappointed in me ...?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: On the Flannan Isles, I tried to tell your story, but everyone only saw it as fiction. They praised its plot and suspense ... But none of the credit really belonged to me.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I failed to unravel the mysteries, and I failed to help people understand arcanum. My so-called dream ... was nothing more than an excuse to run from reality.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I had run, tail tucked, to the Foundation, and then to Vienna ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: In the end, it feels as though I've accomplished nothing.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I couldn't help Madam Hofmann stop Manus Vindictae. I couldn't find the incantation that might grant immunity from the "Storm" ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I only ruin everything!
Yet the bitter chill of remorse fails to tear her down ...
For her loyal friends' warmth, even through the veil of death, can illuminate the darkest nights. Like a refuge on her dark seas.

items.speaker: "James"
items.text: Lass, we don't know what kind of trouble you're facing now, but things are rarely as bad as you fear them to be. Take that on aged wisdom.

items.speaker: "Donald"
items.text: Aye, I'm—no, we're all proud of you!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But ... I didn't do anything helpful for you ...

items.speaker: "Thomas"
items.text: Right, now I won't have you slandering a friend of mine like that, eh? Or did you forget who wrote those wonderful stories what made people remember the Flannan Isles–and us–forever?

items.speaker: "James"
items.text: That may well have been the cleverest thing I've heard you say yet.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But I didn't even uncover the truth behind your deaths. I've failed you all ...
Her head hangs low, with an irrepressible shake lurching her forward and back.

items.speaker: "James"
items.text: Heh heh ...
A familiar touch of warmth reaches Marcus's shoulder again.

items.speaker: "James"
items.text: Now don't be so hard on yourself, lass. How can we blame you if we haven't figured that out for ourselves! With a dozen years head start no less!

items.speaker: "James"
items.text: We've always stayed here all this time, but we've never given up hope. We'll continue to seek out the truth, no matter how long it takes!

items.speaker: "James"
items.text: Remember what Madam Hoffman told you, "Whether you find the truth or not, it is the journey that keeps us engaged."
Suddenly, she is reminded of that edition.
Why was it so loved by her readers?

items.speaker: "James"
items.text: ... You remember those letters from your readers?

items.speaker: "James"
items.text: So many bright ideas, trying to fix the puzzle you set out for them. Nary a one got close, eh? But, remember the fun we had talking them over?

items.speaker: "James"
items.text: Finding the answer is not what really matters, lass. What matters most is our perseverance—our courage to carry on.
Marcus finally lifts her head.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Madam Hofmann ... She understood that lesson all along and tried to pass it on to me.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... But do I really understand it now?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: If I were to die today, would I know what I was supposed to do?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I think ... I do now.
Standing up, she races forward, just like she did on the island coast that fateful day.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "What really scared me was not death, but the possibility of dying ignorant."

items.speaker: Donald
items.text: Marcus, d-did you hear that? It's s-some kind of strange noise ...
She takes a deep breath and opens her eyes.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: We ... we can still make this right.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Doctor, wait! There might be another way!
THE END
Endless Shoreline

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I used to think other people's opinions didn't matter to 37.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Even in the most heated arguments, she never paid them much attention.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: With ordinary eyes, it's difficult to perceive changes in the vastness beyond us.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: But now I understand how to notice them. The faint scrape of fingers brushing over geometry, the different grains of sand I scoop up when I bend over.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: The changes are slow and gradual, but they're there.
Apollo's star had risen high, and the Star of Hermes's game had ended.
It was time to head back to that room filled with scattered papers.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: ... ? 37, what's on your mind?
37's steps were unusually slow. She wondered if the verdict had hit her harder than she predicted.
The ever-scrupulous Corrector began to regret her decision—perhaps it would have been better for 6 to maintain the balance.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: ... Sophia.
37 started somberly, her words flatter than usual.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I hope I didn't waste your time.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Do you think it was all just a pointless game?
The doubts spilled out of her, eagerly awaiting an answer.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Of course not! That song means a lot to me, it's a precious memory.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Are you upset, 37? You didn't seem so down when we listened to the song earlier.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Well, that’s because it had such a lovely cadence, and you sang it so well!
Her praise came sincerely and quickly, no doubt about it.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But what surprised me was when you mentioned that proof about infinite primes ...

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I remember it, but I have no idea when I told you about it.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Of course, I remember, 37. It was a beautiful proof.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I’ll always remember it.
But that didn't comfort her much. Distractedly, 37 grabbed at her hair.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: ... So, have I messed up your memories of Hugh?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Barging in disrupting your memories, and leaving a mess behind ...
Sophia widened her eyes slightly.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: 37, are you still bothered by what 210 said?
She averted her eyes—that was rare.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: ... Hahaha!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Sophia, what's so funny!?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Sorry ...  I just never thought I'd see you care about something he said.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: You're right, you really have changed a lot after all.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Of course! Didn't I tell you that?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: It's not just my height ...  I've even changed where I sit at the table.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: As the distance between me and the table changes, so does the best angle for catching the sun.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I’m not talking about height or seats ...
Sophia shook her head with a soft smile.
It was a gentle, rare, loving gesture.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: 37, do you know why I've never forgotten that proof about infinite primes?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Because it made me ponder such distant things for the first time.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Before, I didn't care about what "eternity" meant; it felt like nothing. Some far away notion.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Now I stand here, fully aware that the island under our feet will one day disappear, washed away like sand by the tide.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: —But I also believe some things will endure, like grains of gold buried in the silt.
The island was vast enough to house an entire school of thought.
Yet it was also so small, a speck in the waves.
And we, living amidst it, could only remember fleeting moments.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Yes, because the world we see is transient.
37 nodded seriously; this topic was more familiar to her than discussing dinner plans.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: You shared it with me because of the eternity and beauty that the infinite holds, and its universally true nature. From then on, I’ve seen the gold in the sands.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: And in turn, I shared Hugh's song with you. If it brought you joy, that means it has meaning for you too.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Maybe it's not the transcendent essence you were seeking. But those who hear the song will feel it, remember it—maybe even hum it one day.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: That is universal beauty too.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: ... ! So that's it—I get it now!
The confusion vanished from 37's face, and she returned all at once to her usual cheerful self.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: This song isn't just for Hugh and Sophia anymore because you shared it with us ...  right?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: So it's universal and belongs to everyone who hears it! Just like the proof I shared with you!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: ... Why are you laughing again, Sophia?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: ... Oh, it’s nothing.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I’m just thinking about how you’re always turning everything into a proof to understand it ...

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: When it's as simple as enjoying music with friends.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: ... Hmm!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I suppose I still can't quite grasp this kind of simplicity ...
37 thought hard about this, puzzling over it like a new problem.
But thankfully, she soon had a new idea, as always.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: "Sharing" is really a solid argument—I bet 210 would struggle to argue against it!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I knew my viewpoint was right! I'm going to tell him right away!
37 hurried off and caught up with 210, who was leafing through another magazine.
What now? Sophia's declared I won and nothing can change that.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: You were just a spectator, making random guesses, while I uncovered a valuable song!
Believe what you want—I've said enough today; I'd like a bit of peace and quiet now.
He deliberately slowed down, trailing behind Sophia and 37.
37 took it as 210 conceding, and her steps became light as air.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Well, except for some trivial details, everything went smoothly today.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: It's the number "9", the trinity of peace, friendship, and harmony. Absolutely perfect.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Oh, that’s right!
37 turned to Sophia with a sudden recollection, a joyful smile spreading across her face.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Come on, Sophia, give me your hand—

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: This is for you.
The feathers, shells, and pebbles formed a lovely decorative chain.
There was a lone pebble next to it.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: ... Is this for me?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Of course! And this one, I found it on the beach just now.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The pattern forms a fantastic number! You can add it to the chain or, you know, give it a toss into the waves!

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Thanks, 37.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I came to the beach this morning to give it to you.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But I found myself sidetracked and completely forgot ...

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: That's alright, 37, I really appreciate your gift.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: That's great! Shall we hang out again tomorrow, Sophia? I'll catch up with my research in no time.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Oh, the day after tomorrow could work too. We could make this a regular island activity—
Now was the time, relaxed and pleasant enough, for her to ask what she had left unsaid.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: 37, do all these numbers have this infinite meaning to you?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Of course.
37 answered without missing a beat.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: So 37 is just one number in the infinite progression?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: If it's not, what else could it be?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: 210, 37, 6 ...  Even if we're gone, these numbers won't disappear.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Just like you don't need three seagulls, three stones, or three people to prove the number three exists.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Numbers exist outside of all that.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Thanks, 37. I think I understand your answer.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I've got some other things to take care of. Let’s hang out later if there's time.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Deal!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Wait, I see 6 coming back!
37 waved at the dot on the horizon, as a seagull swooped above them.
She sprang up, greeting the leader.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Good morning, 6! 210 and I had a disagreement over something ...

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But the sequence, it's connected to a song ...

items.speaker: Six
items.text: I'm afraid I don't know much about songs.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But it's only logical, isn't it?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Is there any doctrine from our past that fits this situation?

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Thinking things through can help purify one’s intellect.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Perhaps a period of quiet contemplation would be helpful.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: That doesn't suit me well, I'm afraid. Alright, I'll come up with more convincing new arguments on my own.
It was clear that 37 wasn't satisfied with 6's suggestion.
The debate would keep going in the coming days.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Watch your step, or you'll trip.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Don’t worry. As long as I stick to the right order of steps, I won't fall!
Don't forget, we've got to hurry or we'll miss mealtime.
That seagull looks as starved as her.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: We could calculate the seagull's speed by counting steps ...

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Where did we stop counting?
You can spend all day counting seagulls on the beach tomorrow.
That could be the topic for my next essay.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Planning to cover up a weak argument with a bunch of superfluous dribble again?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Alright, you two let's pick up the pace.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: There are other ways to figure out its speed.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: 284 steps.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Thanks, 6!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: And the time it took us to get here is ...
THE END
A Golden Key

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I have a small room. It has a simple door.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: The room is cramped. It's a truly tiny little room.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: But besides that simple door, there are many, many other doors in this room. Big ones, small ones; hard ones, soft ones; mushy and wet ones; warm and furry ones.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: They're in front of me. They're behind me. There are so many of them, and more keep coming. They squeeze me.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Do you know how that feels? To be squeezed by many, many doors?
Isolde turns her eyes to you.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I suppose no one in the world has felt what it's like. No one would ever place so many doors in one room.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Door after door lies on me, compressing me until my skin, my flesh, and bones squeak under the pressure. I'm enveloped by endless pain, as if my flesh is being torn from my skeleton.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: When I was a little girl, I read a story about a princess who tried to sleep on a hundred layers of mattresses yet was still kept awake by a single pea beneath them.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: My father called her the true embodiment of a princess, a good maiden with noble virtue and the most delicate skin in the world. He said that I should be such a lady, both sensitive and polite.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: But am I that princess?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Or that bothersome little pea under a hundred mattresses?

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: Baby, my child, my darling ...
Mother hugged me, as she always did when overtaken with despair. Theophil had grown up, and Trista was long gone, so I was her only choice.
The day prior, her hysteria had burst out at a banquet, making her shame all the more potent. That's why she came to my room and held me close.

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: You must always remember Mama's words. Don't you ever forget!

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: You have to be careful. Don't allow others to see your vulnerability. Don't cry, don't scream, don't lose control ... Don't make a fool of yourself.

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: Your true self is filthy. Reveal it, and it will hurt you—even kill you.
Her hands squeezed my arms, quivering. I couldn't help but quiver with her.

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: It will only make you suffer—keep you from your dreams and plunge you into nightmares ...

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: It's a most frightful, terrible beast, and it will tear you apart! Just as it tore me, and your grandmother, and your great grandmother.

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: You must conceal it, Isolde! Not one girl in our cursed family has been able to survive in this world without doing so. You must follow the rules of society.
I didn't fully comprehend what she meant back then. Curses, rules, concealment ... It was all too complicated for a four-year-old child.
So I asked her what it meant, what I should do.
There was a long silence before Mother spoke, so long that I almost fell asleep in her arms.
In my semi-dreamlike state, I heard my mother's voice. It was soft and distant, as if floating down from a cloud.

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: You must learn to play a "role" in life, my little Isolde ...
She brushed my hair with her fingers, her face twisted in agony.
She had been dancing in this pair of hot iron shoes for over twenty years, and in this moment, she presented them to me.

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: You must learn to know what people expect from you. Then, do everything you can to meet those expectations.

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: You'll have to work harder than anyone else to satisfy the people around you so as to make their "tolerance" of you worthwhile ...

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: Smile despite your suffering and breakdowns, and walk steadily, even if your feet are crippled, even if the road ahead seems fine to others but in ruins to you ...
She cupped my face in her hands, kissing my forehead and cheeks. Her tears fell on my face like rain.

She was in so much pain—for me and for herself. It was terrifying to wear that pair of burning iron shoes like that. But it was the only way our ancestors survived. It was the only way we would survive.
And that was the first time I saw a "door." It was small and blue, just the right size for a child like me to pass through.
It squeezed into my room like a cat squeezes through a crack in a door. Eventually, I fell asleep in my mother's arms.
It was not the door to the small room.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: A hundred times. That's right, scoop up the soup one hundred times.
It was then that I saw the second door.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: You've done well, my child. See? Your hands have stopped shaking.
Mr. Karl stood by that door. His figure was formidable.
I kept my distance. I didn't like Mr. Karl.
I respected him, but I feared him. He seemed so tall to me—grander than a palace, more oppressive than a mountain. He haunted my every nightmare.
In those nightmares, he was an entrance to a wide, luxurious ballroom. It was filled with faceless people, all staring at me silently.
Sometimes I was disheveled, barefoot, or naked. But I was always scrambling to cover myself up—to hide my shame.
It's the door to the Dittarsdorf house, and I am the last remaining Dittarsdorf. It is mine alone. Of course it's in the room.
It isn't the door to the small room, either.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Literature.

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: Art.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Poetry. Stage design.

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: Models. Romance.
I've never paid much attention to their conversations, but these words summarize the majority of their topics.

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: Oh? What do you think, Heinrich?
Theophil is an enthusiastic and perhaps "kind-hearted" person.

He understood himself to be a noble man and a brother. I cannot deny that he fulfilled his obligations, nor can I deny his foolishness. He spent his days indulging in his pleasures with blissful decadence.
He brought me gifts, like Mayer's hound brought her its prey.
And his eyes glittered just like the hound's did.
I would thank him and take his gifts, which greatly inspired him to go on the hunt once more.
As I'm sure you can tell, he was easily pleased. We had a simple relationship.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Hey, why don't we start an organization together?

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: I just thought of an excellent name—
Is Heinrich a friend of mine or my brother? How did we even come to be friends?
Our parents were close. He and Theophil grew up together. We'd spent long holidays on each other's estates since we were children.
How time had flown. That little chatterbox had become taller than I.
His fervor for conversation, although sometimes grating, was not without benefit, however. He introduced me to many new faces.

items.speaker: Klara
items.text: That's a superb name! I'd love to join!
It was he who introduced me to her—my new friend.

items.speaker: Playwright
items.text: Salome ...
What can I say about her?
My mother's therapist, the gardener, and Maggie the maid were all her and her father's moles.
Who picked up the trash bags of old handkerchiefs, worn pajamas, and dirty bed sheets that were left outside the gate? Who ate the dead rabbit that signaled my birth?
Does the answer really matter?
They were quiet, sincere, even. They made no demands, no requests.
Like a pebble lying at the bottom of a river or in the gaps of a railroad, they lived in their own world.
They couldn't even stir up a wave, let alone become the straw that broke the camel's back. They impacted no one.
But still, when Mr. Karl's ballroom pressed upon me, so, too, did she slip into my shoe. A small stone. A perpetual annoyance compounding my great pain.

items.speaker: Playwright
items.text: My ... muse ...
It's just as Father said.
"Be generous, my daughter. It is an honor that they love you so much."
"Be lenient. Let them be."

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: Sleep, my darling, safe and sound ...
This is how her story should end, don't you think?

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: My darling baby ... Trista, Isolde ...

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: I keep hearing things ... My heart is broken, my joints are screaming ... no, not my joints, my spleen. It feels as though it's ruptured, and there are a million voices shouting in my head ...

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: What should I do? What should I do!? You need to help me! No, who can help me?
She was in so much distress—so much pain.
My mother, my Evangeline.

She could no longer hold her baby. She could no longer live in the illusion of a forever young Apfelstrudel and Blume. She was like an overfilled glass of wine that finally spilled over, staining the clothes of everyone at the table.

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: This is "salvation" ... My dear, dear ...

items.speaker: Evangeline
items.text: The world is filthy. Just breathing is torturous ...
When she dreamed about Trista, when she saw that sweet smile again, when she relived her death ...
... Mother found the exit of her life.

The door to freedom opened before her.
And she was far too kind to leave behind her husband and maids.
Evangeline followed Trista. Theophil followed Evangeline.
One in water, one in fire—they ended their lives.
Not only had the curse taken Evangeline, but also the two remaining men of the Dittarsdorf family. The curse that had once only plagued my mother's family had truly taken over all the Dittarsdorfs.
People started looking at me with pitiful and prying eyes. Of course, they would gaze at a tragic but wealthy and well-bred girl like that, especially those who had sons of marriageable age.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Oh, my poor Isolde. Why is this happening to you?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: First your father, then your mother, and now Theophil ...
Mr. Karl wiped his tears with a white hankie. His face ruddy and full, like a peach. The sincerity of his response made him almost charming.

Was he always this way?
Where was that stern, harsh gentleman from my memory?
I thanked him, I consoled him, and I shook his hand. This was the Karl my father saw, wasn't it?
I was an adult then. He was treating me as such.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Isolde ... Are you alright?
Luckily, there were some more welcome visitors.
A different kind of friend. A friend who stood by my side, a sincere worried expression on her face.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Call me anytime, no matter how late it is. Don't hesitate, alright?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: By the way, when you were in the house just now, did you notice a door?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: A door? What kind of door?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: It's a door. One of the most common types. No one would notice it was placed in such a big, magnificent mansion.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: It appeared on the evening of my thirteenth birthday.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I vomited on my bed that night. I couldn't digest all that cake and roast chicken. My stomach hurt.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Those wandering spirits bent over me, making funny faces and silently clapping as I heaved up my dinner.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: The guests downstairs were waiting for me. I had to get myself together to go back and thank everyone for celebrating my birthday with me.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: But I was too tired. I hadn't had a good night's sleep in months.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: And that was when I came up with the idea.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I invited the spirits to fall upon me, whether they were willing or not.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I utilized the spirits' proficiencies to do what I couldn't do alone. They helped me flatter my guests, behave well, sing and dance, read and write literature ... They aided me in everything.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I was finally able to rest.
Theophil's funeral is over. More than half of the servants have been let go. Ms. Dittasdorf says she needs some time alone and refuses to receive any visitors.
Isolde crosses the living room, walking straight to the sideboard.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Maggie isn't home, so there's no one to take care of Blume, Apfelstrudel, and the nightingale and swan ...
She opens the drawer and takes out a metal box of arsenic powder.
It has been the most deadly poison since the time of ancient Rome until today.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: They're my responsibility now.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Here, Apfelstrudel, Blume, come have some ...
She carries the box over to the tea table by the window and places the box on it.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Be graceful, be self-restrained, and be kind to others.
She tilts the tea pot and watches the tea flow into the cup.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Be compassionate, especially towards the less privileged.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: There's nothing to be afraid of. You have the right to leave this ruined world ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: We ... must be an example for our people.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Oh dear, you're twitching ... It's alright. I'll hold you.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: We must ...
Isolde drops her eyes. The arsenic powder dissolves in the hot tea as if it had never existed.
She raises the tea cup and slightly lowers her head.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: We must be virtuous and dignified, as befits our status, Theophil.
In the tea cup, her charred brother gazes at her sorrowfully.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Ah ... How careless I am. I almost forgot the date today.
She raises her head and throws the tea cup over her shoulder, splashing her brother's face on the floor.
She picks up her coat from the hanger and walks toward the porch, muttering to herself.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: My new doctor, my Kakania ... Dr. Kakania.
Clinic Doorway

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Oh, it appears I've arrived a little early.
It is good etiquette for a lady to arrive early to an appointment.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: That's alright. I can wait. I have patience.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Ms. Kakania ... Oh, I suppose I should call her Dr. Kakania from now on.
She looks up at the closed door.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: There's no sign indicating that this is the consultation room ... Oh, right, she doesn't have a medical license.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Ah, so she's painted the door this color so that the patients can tell where she is. How very clever.
As she waits, Isolde murmurs softly to herself.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: There are so many doors in this world.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Is Dr. Kakania a door, too? What kind of door would she be, I wonder?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Would it be green or shining like silk? Perhaps ...
She is interrupted by a familiar voice.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Hmm? Isolde?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Sorry, I'm late!
Kakania trots over to her, her lively green skirt swaying with each step.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I was delayed. You know what I'm like. I swear I'd planned to return earlier to ensure this didn't happen! This is our first consultation, after all! Oh, I so wanted to have a good start to our doctor-patient relationship!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm really, very sorry. Have you been waiting long?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Are you tired? Oh, I shouldn't have kept you waiting under the sun ...
As Kakania continues her apologies, she pulls a golden key with a green ribbon from her waist.
A golden key to the golden lock on the door. She inserts it and turns it. The door opens.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Alright, come on in! I'll fetch you a cup of tea.
Kakania enters the side room. Isolde can see her cheerful green dress reflected in the corner of the mirror as she busies herself with the tea.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I'm looking forward to it.
There she is, reflected in the Vingler's Mirror, the daughter of a mirror seller. Klara. Dr. Kakania.
She's not a door. I was wrong. Very wrong.
She is a key.
The key that will finally unlock my door.
THE END
Ruinas Gloriosas
Wasteland - Night
On that pitch-black night, Recoleta sees no one.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Why am I back in the desert? Where did Hunting go?

items.speaker: Gaucho Rider
items.text: You've drunk the poisoned wine, Recoleta. A treacherous scheme of the cave dwellers.

items.speaker: Gaucho Rider
items.text: It's the venom of the ouroboros's fangs, severing the cause-and-effect leading us to the Ruinas Gloriosas.
In her mind, her own voice echoes.

items.speaker: Gaucho Rider
items.text: They tried to stop us, but fortunately, they didn't know that we are one and the same.

items.speaker: Gaucho Rider
items.text: I left Directrices de Metáforas in your notebook. It will lead you to the final ending.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: You took the poison for me? But why? Why did you sacrifice yourself? Haven't you longed to see the victory of our great movement?

items.speaker: Gaucho Rider
items.text: No more questions. It was a necessary sacrifice.

items.speaker: Gaucho Rider
items.text: I did it for us. Now, go. Save our comrades and see this journey through to the very end!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I understand now. The comrade you're talking about is Hunting, isn't it?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I need to find the Ruinas Gloriosas and free her.
Recoleta snaps back to reality, pushes herself to her feet, and strides forward with determination.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: "Cross the silent desert, follow the Gnostic River to its source. A forgotten river runs, its course to all untold ..."

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: "At the source of the Gnostic River, in shrouded darkness laid, within that mirror, the cave dweller hides, his ancient face displayed."

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: So I just need to follow this river, right?
Gnostic River Source

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Phew, what a long night. Looks like I've finally found the source of the Gnostic River.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: And now? There's no other path forward.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Wait. Could it be ...?
