"Within that mirror ..." Recoleta gazes at the black surface of the water.
She pinches her nose shut and leaps in.
Recoleta feels herself sliding downward through a cave, yet there is no sense of wetness or flowing water.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Whoa ... Waaaah! ... Haha, waaah!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Wee! Hahaha! This is actually kind of fun!
Cave
She lands in a misty, damp cavern.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: "Tread lightly, do not disturb those shadowed tribal dwellers. Their language is as unyielding as stone, their gazes deep as caverns."

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: The cave dwellers ... Are they those figures wandering around?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Can they really see me? Their eyes look completely vacant. Maybe I don't need to hide at all.

items.speaker: Cave Dweller I
items.text: Grant me immortality!

items.speaker: Cave Dweller II
items.text: Grant me glory!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Aah! Stay away from me!
Recoleta takes off running, ignoring everything as she sprints forward.
After passing through countless identical caves, Recoleta finally stops to listen. No footsteps, only the sound of an inexplicable underground wind.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Phew, finally lost them. That wasn't so bad.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Let's see, the next line says ..."The ninth and tenth time darkness falls, Las Ruinas Gloriosas shall appear—to mark the journey's end, in ruined glory and radiance, clear."

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: So, am I supposed to sleep down here for over a week to unlock the next puzzle?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Wait. I see! This is a puzzle too!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: This place is still lit! So, to make "darkness fall," I need to extinguish all these braziers.
The flames instantly go out, as if responding directly to Recoleta's thoughts.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Alright, one more. On to the next cave.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Hmm, if my count is right, this should be the tenth cave.
There is no path ahead, only a thick, gray mist.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: "To mark the journey's end"—so that mist must be it? I see. I need to complete the "ninth and tenth time" to reach the tenth night.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: But, "ninth and tenth" ... What does that even mean? What if I extinguish the last fire in this tenth cave?
Recoleta sits cross-legged, staring at the final brazier.
After a long pause, she suddenly laughs, then picks up the brazier with both hands.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: It must be this brazier! It marks the boundary between the ninth cave and the tenth.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Wow. These metaphors and symbols really are hard to understand. I think I finally get why people struggle with my novels.
With all her strength, she hurls the flames into the mist.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Go! Bring forth the light!
The Ruinas Gloriosas
The mist scatters. Ahead, four enormous phantoms loom.
Behind them, she barely makes out a shackled figure in the darkness.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Ms. Hunting?! Are you alright?
Hunting seems to be speaking, but an unseen barrier muffles her voice.

items.speaker: "Numb"
items.text: I tried to stop you, but you still came.

items.speaker: "Enlighten"
items.text: Child, why must you seek the secret of the "Ageless"?

items.speaker: "Cheering"
items.text: Executioner, your cruelty has broken my heart!

items.speaker: "Slighted"
items.text: How amusing. I never thought you'd make it here.
Countless voices echo in the ruins, mocking her powerlessness.
And four voices rise in unison, forming a harmony.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Step aside. I must rescue my comrade!
Recoleta faces the phantom symbols like a knight, her pen wielded like a sword.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Clearly, this battle isn't about strength. You are not the Minotaur guarding the labyrinth. You are mere obstacles, symbols created to hinder me.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Las Ruinas Gloriosas—the answer's in the name, right?

items.speaker: Symbolic Chorus
items.text: Clever little writer, what blocks your path is nothing but imaginary chains.

items.speaker: Symbolic Chorus
items.text: With the mere flick of your pen, you may sever them. It is unbelievably simple!
Recoleta lunges forward with her sword. In the darkness, the sounds of chains snapping ring out. But before long, more chains, newborn and endless, emerge from the abyss.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: What ... What's going on?!
Recoleta slashes over and over again through the chains, but her efforts are in vain. Exhausted, she collapses to the ground.
A flickering shadow catches the corner of her eye. It's Hunting, off in the distance. What is she doing?
Hunting has abandoned words. She raises both hands above her head, outlining a rectangle.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: A rectangle. What's that supposed to mean?
Hunting makes a motion as if embracing something, tracing the shape of the rectangle repeatedly in the air.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: A ... pillar? Wait ... the pillar from before!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: It's the pillar del Templo de la Metáfora!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: ... The MacGuffin?!

items.speaker: Editor Hunting
items.text: "In crook stories, it is almost always the necklace ..."
Those quoted words strike Recoleta like lightning in a spring storm.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Yes, a necklace—a chain! Just like the Templo de la Metáfora. These chains are meaningless! I need to move past them and face the core of Ruinas Gloriosas head-on.
Countless chains bind and drag Recoleta to the ground under their weight. She covers her ears, struggling as she steps into the four symbols.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: East, West, South, North!
Recoleta swings her sword in all four directions. With each strike, she bears the weight of a thousand chains.
The twisted laughter fades. Exhaustion and relief wash over her, and she collapses to the ground.
Her eyelids feel unbearably heavy. Hunting's voice grows distant.
The Pampas Plain
The cowboy gazes out the window at the prairie, the fresh green of spring filling her with an almost dreamlike sense of renewal.

items.speaker: Cowboy
items.text: My head hurts a little. Maybe I slept too long.

items.speaker: Cowboy
items.text: Those adventures seem hazy now.

items.speaker: Coachman
items.text: It's alright. You've already written our adventures into a novel.

items.speaker: Coachman
items.text: We escaped the Templo de la Metáfora, wandered for ages in the Symbolic Forest, and in the end, you saved me in the Ruinas Gloriosas.
The cowboy feels as if she's in a dream, but she knows the coachman is right. Those images slowly resurface in her mind.

items.speaker: Cowboy
items.text: Alright. And my novel? Is it finished?

items.speaker: Coachman
items.text: Have you forgotten? We wrote an eternal masterpiece and even won a significant literary award!

items.speaker: Cowboy
items.text: Where are we going?

items.speaker: Coachman
items.text: We're heading home.

items.speaker: Coachman
items.text: Back to Buenos Aires, back to the H.A. Publishing House for a grand award ceremony.

items.speaker: Coachman
items.text: And then, our story will come to an end.
The cowboy chuckles softly.
She waves at the tall figure before her.
As the carriage jostles forward, she throws open the door and leaps into the golden light of the sun.

items.speaker: Cowboy
items.text: Goodbye, Ms. Hunting!

items.speaker: Cowboy
items.text: Publishing novels, receiving awards ... None of that matters to me anymore.

items.speaker: Cowboy
items.text: There's a whole beautiful world before me! Shouldn't I live like a poet and go out and experience its wonders under the glorious radiance of Apollo? Shouldn't I run free, feeling the grass and earth between my toes?

items.speaker: Cowboy
items.text: After all, the story is far from over.
Behind her, the coachman—Hunting—watches, relief and longing coloring her face.
She waves at the soaring figure of freedom.

items.speaker: Editor Hunting
items.text: You're as careless as ever, Recoleta! You forgot that, in the story, you're supposed to call me Coachman!

items.speaker: Editor Hunting
items.text: But none of that matters now. Go, Recoleta!

items.speaker: Editor Hunting
items.text: Like an invincible warrior, like a falcon soaring free, like a fearless Gaucho Knight! Go forth and conquer the boundless Pampas Plain!

items.speaker: Editor Hunting
items.text: Good luck, rebellious, nameless writer who scorns fame and disregards all else!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Blessed me, blessed me, my beating heart does drum—the fervent words of visceral realism, within my chest they thump.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Come on home, spirits of the past!
Editorial Director's Office
The seasons cycle once more.
And a new winter arrives.
Hunting sits at her desk, warming her hands with a cup of coffee as she flips through a manuscript.

items.speaker: Editor Hunting
items.text: You need to dissect the salesman's psychology more deeply. Everything else is fine. If we're lucky, it might be published before spring.

items.speaker: Writer Thomas
items.text: Hmm? In the past, you'd have said, "No one cares about a retired salesman's story."

items.speaker: Editor Hunting
items.text: True. But things have changed. Just like Gregor Samsa in The Metamorphosis. You just need to write as well as Kafka, Tommy.

items.speaker: Writer Thomas
items.text: May I ask—what made you leave such a high-paying job to start your own publishing house?

items.speaker: Editor Hunting
items.text: That's a secret, a secret ... which has a little something to do with you.

items.speaker: Writer Thomas
items.text: Oh? You mean my novel moved you that much?!
A knock at the door interrupts the writer.

items.speaker: Publishing House Employee
items.text: I'm sorry to intrude, Director. We received a package—an anonymous novel addressed to you.

items.speaker: Editor Hunting
items.text: Let me take a look.
The employee unwraps the package and gently places a thin booklet on the desk.

items.speaker: Writer Thomas
items.text: Ah, Ruinas Gloriosas y Directrices de Metáforas by Recoleta—

items.speaker: Writer Thomas
items.text: That's ...?

items.speaker: Writer Thomas
items.text: Ms. Hunting, are you alright?

items.speaker: Editor Hunting
items.text: ... Phew.

items.speaker: Editor Hunting
items.text: She put the dedication in the preface. Looks like she still remembers my advice.
THE END
Abandoned Village
After a short rest, the team disperses into the abandoned village. The Manus followers have retreated quickly, as if they anticipated the current scene.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: That's odd.
How long ago had the singing stopped?
When the long-lost silence descended again, it somehow felt a little ... out of place.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Did it disappear during the battle just now?
Perhaps, for only then could it have disappeared without her noticing.
The return of Emil interrupts Semmelweis’ pondering.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Captain!

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Did you find anything?

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Following your indications, we found a secret chamber nearby.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: The chamber bears traces of a traveler's brief stay. It's clear that the Manus Vindictae were there.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Take me there.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Based on the traces of arcane skills, we believe they were rescued in the chaos of the battle just now.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Hmm ... Are there others who are trying to rescue the prisoner too?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I see ... The refugees used us.
Despite this realization, Semmelweis’ face shows no sign of discontent.
The room is modest, with only a small window connecting it to the outside world.
It is simply decorated, with few noteworthy features.
Semmelweis notices an envelope on the desk.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Is this ... a letter?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Did the Manus Vindictae leave it for me? Or perhaps it was ...

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: ... the prisoner.
The answer to this question is not hard to find; all she has to do is open the letter.
Semmelweis reaches out and picks up the letter from the table.
The ink has not yet dried. Clearly, the sender left not long ago.
The letter is not long—just a few lines.
However, Semmelweis reads it several times, searching for any hint of the Manus Vindictae's whereabouts.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Is this ... some sort of hallucination?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: —No, it can't be.
If this was indeed a hallucination, it was so realistic as to be indiscernible from reality.
Semmelweis takes a deep breath and calms herself. She doesn't want Emil to notice her heightened state.
She examines the letter again, word by word.
“Hello, unknown visitor.”
“I know a way to cure your condition and keep you alive.”
“That's right, I have a method to help you survive the affliction given to you by the infected.”
“Please find me in Vienna. Then, you will find redemption and overcome impurity.”
There is a signature at the bottom.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Lorelei from the Rhine.
Who is this person? How does she know all this?
Semmelweis' biggest secret is written so plainly, like an open menu awaiting the scrutiny of a customer.
Countless questions begin to swirl in her mind.
For a scholar, “the infected” is too broad a term. It encompasses countless failures and few survivors.
Therefore, in arcanum, there is a more precise and direct way to refer to this disease that almost exclusively affects arcanists.
The Beyond Disease.
That is the true name of Semmelweis' affliction.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Captain, what's wrong? You've been staring at that letter for a while ...

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: This letter contains certain classified information that I intend to pass on to the Foundation.
Semmelweis calmly removes her comm from its case and calls Madam Lindsay.
Seeing this, Emil asks no more questions. He leaves the room.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay.
items.text: Semmelweis, what's the status on the mission?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Everything went smoothly, Madam Lindsay. I was just about to report the details. We—

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay.
items.text: No, the debriefing can be postponed.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay.
items.text: There's now an urgent mission of even greater importance.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay.
items.text: Investigator Hofmann in Vienna has requested the assistance of the Field Agent Administration.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay.
items.text: Unfortunately, the other squads are unable to reach Vienna in the required time.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Vienna...
“Please find me in Vienna. Then, you will find redemption and overcome impurity.”

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I understand. I have two “Teleport” arcane skill floppy disks. They'll help me reach Vienna quickly.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay.
items.text: I promise you, this is your last mission in this era.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay.
items.text: When you return, the medical department will talk to you again about your condition.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Madam Lindsay, Hofmann is my friend, too. I'm glad for the opportunity to help her.
Upon ending the communication, Semmelweis places the communication device back into her backpack, just as she had done countless times before.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: “Lorelei from the Rhine” ...
—Semmelweis mutters, looking towards Vienna.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Is this also fate's doing?
THE END
Laplace Rehabilitation Center
A familiar location.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: We meet again.
The doctor pushes up his glasses and smiles kindly.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: You still haven’t given up?

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: You should know that your struggle is meaningless.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: Neither the Foundation nor those witch doctor arcanists can do anything about your condition.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: Even before the "Storm", the Foundation had few options for dealing with this condition.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: They have even fewer now.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: Perhaps you’d like me to recount the data?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I know perfectly well what’s happening now.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Arcanists infected with the Beyond Disease will face a physical and mental breakdown.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: The hallucinations and pain will destroy them from the inside out. Less than 5% of arcanists survive the process.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Those arcanists who are lucky enough to make it through to the other side are called "the infected".

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: The majority of them will be plagued by mental illness for the rest of their lives.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Did I miss anything?

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: You seem to know what’s going on, “Rotten Wand”.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: You should be grateful for your little bit of arcanist blood.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: It's given you that 5% chance that you wouldn’t have if you were human.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: But, should you really be grateful?

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: You’re like an ignorant hunter who greedily pursues the white stag, charging headlong into a swamp.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: Isn’t it better to hurry back to the Foundation and accept your final moments?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: The Foundation will help me. I've never questioned that.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Which is also why I can’t sit and wait for death there.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I'll use my remaining time to contribute to the Foundation and pay them back for all they’ve done for me.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: It seems you're more inclined to die in the "Storm" like a stray dog than to enjoy your last moments in peace.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: You’re in over your head, trying to fight destiny. Little do you know, your actions are just a line in the footnote of fate.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: ... Perhaps my mind has become deranged as a result of the infection; maybe I’ve snapped—

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But you cannot shake my determination. After all, you’re just a hallucination.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: A hallucination? No. You’ll understand soon. It’s not that simple.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: You were never special, Semmelweis.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: You’re just an ordinary person who can’t even use arcane skills.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: What makes you think you’re special? What makes you think you can defeat destiny?

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: —You’ll simply disappear into history. Just like the scum who don’t survive to be called "infected".

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: Alright, you can go. Today’s treatment is finished.
The scene shifts. By the time Semmelweis comes to her senses, she has left the hallucination.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: ... He was boring.
She lowers her head to examine her hands.
They're beginning to fade away, becoming transparent. She can see the light shining through her palms and hitting the ground beneath.
Intense pain tears at the gaps between bone and flesh, as if the two are trying to rend themselves from one another.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: The breakdown of my mind and body is accelerating.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Is it because of the singing ...?
Since the singing started, the symptoms of the Beyond Disease have rapidly increased in intensity.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Captain, are you ... Are you okay?
Emil looks worried.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Does the letter say anything special?

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Since you first looked at it, you’ve been in a daze—oh, I mean, thinking.
Semmelweis looks down at the letter in her hand.
“Hello, unknown visitor.”
“I know a way to cure your condition and keep you alive.”
“That's right, I have a method to help you survive the affliction given to you by the infected.”
“Please find me in Vienna. Then, you will find redemption and overcome impurity.”
Lorelei from the Rhine.
After looking at the letter for a while, Semmelweis smiles.
She grasps the paper on both sides ...
... and tears it in half.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Captain?!
Fold, tear. Fold, tear. Fold, tear.
She continues until the letter is nothing but an unreadable pile of scraps.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Emil.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: ... C-Captain?
Emil looks baffled. It isn't like Semmelweis to behave so irrationally.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I don’t care about your betrayal, Emil.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: W-what do you mean, Captain? I don’t understand.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: As a field agent team captain, being prepared for betrayal from within is a must. I saw this coming.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: W-wait, Captain, are you joking? Was the rumor actually true?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Don’t worry, I don't intend on using “that method”. There's no need to go that far.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Evidence indicates that the prisoner, “Lorelei from the Rhine”, left during the battle with the Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: In order for her to leave so smoothly, someone must have helped her.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: And for someone to pull off this operation with such precision and leave a letter, they obviously knew where we were.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Wait, Captain, surely you don't suspect me, do you?! Do you really think I’m passing information to “Lorelei from the Rhine”?

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Captain, I-I'm completely loyal to the Foundation. How could I do something like that?
Semmelweis ignores him, her words calmly cutting through his wailing.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Therefore, when I saw this letter, I came to a conclusion.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: There must be a spy on the team. One who is feeding information to the enemy.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: And most of the refugees we're tracking are from your home country—Serbia.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Please believe me, Captain! I have no ill intent towards you! I just, I just—!

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Though uncommon, this isn't unheard of in the Field Agent Association.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Argh, I never should have helped them in the first place! This confounded letter ... Damn arcanists! Unreliable little—

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: So, are you one of these refugee rescuers?

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: No, no, no! I’m not! I’m a human for crying out loud! How could I have anything to do with those arcanists?

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: I just ... Just happened to assist them!

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: I tipped them off, told them we were going to take care of this team of Manus followers, and that was it!

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: I had no idea what they were up to!

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Why did you do it? As you said, you’re a human and have no reason to help them.
Emil is silent for a moment. Then he heaves a sigh.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Along the way, I was thinking about what you said earlier.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: You said that neither the Foundation nor the Austro-Hungarian Empire could quickly eliminate the influence of Manus Vindictae on the refugees.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Do you know what that means?

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: It means the Austro-Hungarian Empire has to deal with the problems posed by the refugees as quickly as possible.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: The Empire is well aware of the damage a group of unstable arcanists can do.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: So, when the arcanist refugees can't be controlled, the Empire isn't averse to taking extreme measures.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Just like they did in the past.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: After all, they bear no moral responsibility for them.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Yep. It's a common practice these days.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: They're my countrymen. I can't sit back and watch a tragedy like this unfold. I have to find a way to stop it.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Believe me, I have no sympathy for arcanists. They're to blame for all of this.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: But even so, they shouldn't suffer such a fate.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Even if they are Manus scum, they should be judged and punished by the law. Their fates shouldn’t be determined by the whims of old men!
Emil spits on the ground, venting his discontent.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: I don’t know who “Lorelei from the Rhine” really is. But what I do know is that she can stop the refugees from turning to Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: And that’s enough.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: All this careful exploration and tolerance ... It's not making any difference! It's time to do something.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I understand your motivations.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I must say, your behavior surprises me a bit, Emil.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I thought you really hated arcanists.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Everyone hates arcanists. But they're still people—people who live side by side in this world with me!

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: There’s something I neglected to tell you. I’m also an arcanist.
Emil raises his head in disbelief.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Impossible. Why would the Foundation send an arcanist to ...?
Emil trails off, quickly realizing something much more important.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Hang on! Captain, what I mean to say is ... Uh, arcanists are good people, too ...
Semmelweis can’t help but laugh.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Look at me, Emil.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: Captain?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I’m not going to punish you.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: While you have taken advantage of our organization, investigating Manus Vindictae falls within our scope of work.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Besides, this is rather important intelligence.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: So, I'll hide what you’ve done from the higher-ups.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: C-captain—A-are you serious?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Reporting your actions would serve no purpose. It would only cost me a team member.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: T-thank you so much, Captain! I-I ...
Semmelweis’ communication device buzzes.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Good timing. It’s a dispatch from the higher-ups.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: If you’re worried, you can listen in on the call.

items.speaker: Emil
items.text: N-no, I trust you, Captain!
Semmelweis is not lying. She does not intend to report Emil’s actions to Madam Lindsay.
To her, it makes no sense.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Everything went smoothly, Madam Lindsay. I was just about to report the details. We—
The critical point of the era has emerged, which means the arrival of the "Storm" is imminent.
Upon its arrival, the "Storm" will wipe out his existence completely.
There is no need for her to do anything.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: You mean Vienna?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I understand. I have two “Teleport” arcane skill floppy disks. They'll help me reach Vienna quickly.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Madam Lindsay, Hofmann is my friend, too. I'm glad for the opportunity to help her.
Upon ending the communication, Semmelweis places the communication device back into her backpack, just as she had done countless times before.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: “Lorelei from the Rhine”?
—Semmelweis mutters, looking towards Vienna.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Perhaps ... It’s destiny.
THE END

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Doctor, you must stop using the mirror!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: You will both collapse if you continue to force her!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm running out of options.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I have to hypnotize her.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Hypnotize me? Hahaha ... You, Ms. Klara, the doctor who resents hypnosis and had even fought a duel to stop it ... you are going to use it ... on me?!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Why? Because I'm a hysterical, irrational woman? The wicked witch? The cursed, inconsolable arcanist?!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Why, why are you like this to me?!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Please calm yourself, Isolde.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And fix your eyes on this watch.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Why?! Did I do something wrong again? Am I hopelessly incurable?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Why, why couldn't you, cure me?!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Can't you ... save me from despair ... one more time ...?
She looks at the beautiful girl, her once-friend.
But she doesn't know how to save her.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Sleep, Isolde.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: To the peaceful place, to the home of night.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: You're the cruelest of all ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: If you've made up your mind and think I'm guilty ... Why do you treat me so gently?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: If this is the salvation you brought ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I will ... embrace it with joy.
She begins a familiar aria, singing with all her heart.
Her voice at last not some guise or act, but her true self.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I adorned the Madonna's mantle with jewels.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: And I gave my song to the stars, to the sky, which smiled more beautifully because of it.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: In the hour of sorrow.
Why, oh why, Lord.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Why do you repay me thus?
The song never left her.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Look, doctor ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: The stars ... are shining ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Now, tell me, Isolde.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What do you think of when you look at this painting?
Images appear in the mirror.
Clear, bright, and accompanied by the echo of the tide.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I am intrigued by the name of your little group. "The Circle" ...

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: Yes, unlike other animals, there's a power in every one of us. It's the source of our instinct. Following it, man survived the cruelty of nature.

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: In awe of this extraordinary power, the first of man drew a magical circle on the ground, symbolizing a higher power, and declaring that man would no longer be at the mercy of nature.

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: That was the first circle. The first magic, the first art!

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Heh heh ...

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: An interesting take.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: I happened to have a circle too.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: This is also an ancient miracle, a circle of salvation.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: It shelters the chosen ones from the falling rain,

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: and sees them to the promised land.
A vague murmur emanates from the mirror.
Like an ancient echo.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Yes! That's it!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I saw it! Doctor! I heard it!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I "read" the "Storm" immunity ritual! We did it!!!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Finally ...
Kakania falls to the ground, exhausted.
Marcus, ready now to face the communicator again, activates it.
This time, though, it brings good news.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: News from the frontline. They have sent home the "Storm" immunity ritual.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Get to work, people.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: In the 22 hours before the "Storm" arrives, the whole world is our proving ground.
THE END
The days that follow are calm.
The believers, seeking truth and knowledge, sail out to explore a world of constantly changing phenomena.
But the ship's return is far later than expected.

items.speaker: Believer I
items.text: No ... impossible, they are already well past the maximum deviation possible. They must return today ...

items.speaker: Believer I
items.text: As long as they are alive and on the ship, there’s no way they cannot be headed back ...
They wait day and night by the coast, eagerly anticipating the return of their leader and the ship.
Soon, they grow increasingly panicked.

items.speaker: Believer II
items.text: Hey - look, that's the ship!
Until one person shouts excitedly, jumping high with the joyful news.

items.speaker: Believer I
items.text: I knew it, I knew they were alright!

items.speaker: Believer II
items.text: I’m so glad–
The ship returns from its voyage along its planned route, with no deviation in angle or speed.
People run to the coast, waiting to welcome new insights from the outside world, believing these unprecedented ideas will illuminate the path of truth.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Dad—!
Among them is Atticus's dear friend.
The "emanation" descends upon them.
Everyone is calling out; everyone is in an uproar. They scream, cry, and fall to the sandy ground.
The ominous noise even reaches the roofed room.
Ignoring his trembling fingers, Atticus takes the book and opens it on the table.
Regardless of the worst outcome, this is what he had planned to do.

items.speaker: Atticus
items.text: "A voice from the above spoke to a man."

items.speaker: Atticus
items.text: An important thing will happen to you.

items.speaker: Atticus
items.text: What will it be? The man asked.

items.speaker: Atticus
items.text: You will gain wealth, you will gain fame. You will walk in the garden of wisdom and happiness. The voice answered ...
The reading voice stops. His fingers lingering on the page.
At the same time, a geometric shape washes ashore.
It's a beautiful tetrahedron, brilliant with a golden hue like Alma's shining blonde hair when she was in good health.
—The "revelation" has knocked on his door.
Countless ancient knowledge is conveyed through the imprint of the Soul Number 6.
Moral, historical, empirical, abstract, mathematical, humanistic.
This is the crystallization of wisdom passed down from generation to generation by the island's leaders, a glimpse of the mysteries transmitted through the bloodline by those who perceive the truth.
Revelation, knowledge, wisdom —
They surge so tumultuously and vastly that entire lifetimes of achievements and thoughts from mortals are like bottles of water compared to the mighty ocean.
The boulder of fate has rolled down from its peak, and a new 6 is born.
The reef remains unchanged. It has been hardened by the erosive force during the long night.
The paused hand gently falls and turns the page.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: "Revelation" ...

items.speaker: Six
items.text: It is just as simple as it is.
THE END

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Áddjá, white bones ...

items.speaker: Rolf
items.text: Look what you've found, ráhkis.
Four weathered bone fragments lie amid the wild tundra grass.

items.speaker: Rolf
items.text: Here's a vertebra, a rib, a small piece of leg bone ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Áddjá, what was it?
The lean scholar and his young grandchild stand together in a vast and silent expanse. He wipes his glasses with his sleeve, then moves closer to examine the bones.

items.speaker: Rolf
items.text: Most of them have weathered away ... It's hard to say, but judging by their size, it could be a reindeer.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: W-Why didn't the Mother Spirit protect it?
He smiles at her naive question.

items.speaker: Rolf
items.text: *chuckle* ... She doesn't work that way, ráhkis.

items.speaker: Rolf
items.text: This is the cycle of life. See?
Around the bones, where the flesh has rotted away, daisies now bloom. The wind has carried away the rest, scattering it across distant lands and seas.

items.speaker: Rolf
items.text: Nautika, this is the world's smallest miracle ... and its greatest.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I know! It's from Tales of the Mother Spirit, the part that says ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: In death we freed our tired, tattered flesh; And return life's power to nature's mesh. The rain and wind, our heralds, call us home; To Mother's arms—we rest, no more to roam.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: When I return to Her arms, I want to ask Her something.

items.speaker: Rolf
items.text: About what?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I want to know how Her miracle works. How She keeps life turning in the endless cycle.

items.speaker: Rolf
items.text: That curiosity of yours is admirable.

items.speaker: Rolf
items.text: And what will you do once you know this information?
The child pauses. Her innocence has left her unprepared for such a question.
But then, a pure desire spills forth.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Then ... I'll learn Her secret and understand another part of Her.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: In this reindeer's next life, I'll protect it.
She stares at the reindeer's bones and, in the boundlessness of her imagination, makes a small wish.

items.speaker: Rolf
items.text: Hahaha.

items.speaker: Rolf
items.text: Very well, Nautika.

items.speaker: Rolf
items.text: May the Mother Spirit guide you until your soul returns to Her embrace.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Áddjá ...
A long time passes before she realizes that she's no longer in a memory. Her grandfather's phantom hangs just out of reach.
She staggers toward him, still holding on to hope.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Áddjá ... you knew, didn't you? You'd already seen the answer back then.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: That's why you didn't want me to face this final ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: But that's the answer.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Even so, I will pursue the unknown no matter where it takes me.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I know you understand, Áddjá.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Because no one knows me like you do.
The phantom doesn't stir. Until, after what feels like an eternity, a smile of relief crests his lips.
He embraces her and whispers a single word.
And the phantom is gone.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: ... Let's go.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Will you stay with me till the end?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: ... Dagny?
She moves toward the exit, while true memories drift back to her like snow settling in her open palms.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Dagny ... Dagny.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Aase and Áddjá said that you wouldn't last long. But I refused to believe it. I thought if I gave you a name, we could keep you.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I carved a tag for you, whispered your name with every stroke—but by the time I tried to fasten it ... you were already gone.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Then the very next day, Áddjá and I buried you beneath the sapling. Then I carved your name again.
Dagny remains still.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Yes, Dagny, my little reindeer. I never ate you, and we never won any race.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: You followed the cycle—stayed with us for those last moments of your life, then left forever.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Even so, there were so many nights when I thought of you, so many days when your name came to me.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Oh, how I've missed you.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: You were my first adventure. My missing piece, the forest fossil I never found.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: The beginning of everything.
She speaks the truth of this long-departed friend, finding that her words have sound once more.
The calf lingers, gazing into the distance. This is the final revelation.
Then, she bows her head and dissolves into the darkness.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Goodbye ... Dagny.
She turns to the last path.
There, a pool blacker than darkness itself waits at the edge of the void.
This time, she doesn't hesitate. She wades in, slow and resolute.
She reaches the edge of the darkness and peers into the unfathomable water.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I crossed coastlines and glaciers, escaped a maze, climbed snowy mountains ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I went beyond an illusion, refused a passage to the light, and walked free from false memories.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I came here ... for an answer. That's all.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: The one true answer.
She shivers. Her voice chokes.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: The path we chose because of our longing, the destination we thought would fulfill our lives—

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: What's at the end of this road?
She touches the darkness, waiting for its response.
Only silence. Only darkness.
Nothingness.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Aah ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Ah ... ah ...
When reality confirms her premonition, all that remains is pure sorrow.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: So that's the answer ...
Tears stream.
Drop by drop, rippling in the pitch-black pool.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Áddjá ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: What we sought ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Then ... I'll learn Her secret and understand another part of Her.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: In this reindeer's next life, I'll protect it.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: When I learn this secret ... when I know the answer ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I'll understand a part of Her.
Images appear in the dark water.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: And now that I have ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Now I've reached the edge of nothingness; now I've seen that the answer is emptiness itself ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I became a part of it.
The reflection in the water is clearer now. She wipes the tears from her eyes.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: This isn't the end. Not anymore.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Not my end.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Not my final answer.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I have to keep going—to find a new answer, a new meaning ... for who I am now and for who I'll one day be.
The reflection extends a wordless invitation to her.
Even as she wipes her last tears away, fresh ones fall.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I'll keep moving forward ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Even so, I will pursue the unknown no matter where it takes me.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Friele, Aase ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: You don't need to wander anymore. I'll be here.
Tearfully, she smiles—just like the reflection in the water.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Come back to me ...
She's determined.
Her consciousness breaks free from the eroding waves of darkness, flickering with a renewed, if faint, glow.
A light that comes from within.
Then, toward her reflection, she leaps into the depths of the pool.
THE END

items.speaker: Razor
items.text: Phew ... Ugh ...

items.speaker: Razor
items.text: Nicely done, Semmelweis.

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: Oh, my friends! I'm so happy for you! You did it!

items.speaker: Razor
items.text: Although it's clear you were holding back. Still, I couldn't have done it without you.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Forgive me, I need to save some energy in case I have to deal with the "Scorching Heart" arcane skill.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: I won't do that. That would be tantamount to abandoning my colleagues in their time of need.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Actually, I'd prefer to take matters into my own hands, Madam Lindsay.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Need I remind you how you used the Field Agent Squads?

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: That was a necessary tactic.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: Either way, you should be grateful.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: I just received an order from the higher-ups at the Foundation.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: The order states that I'm to take you and the arcanist called Lorelei back to the Foundation.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: Wasn't that your goal, Semmelweis?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I simply demonstrated my and Lorelei's worth to the Foundation—a living Infected and an arcanist with a unique arcane skill ...

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: The Foundation would never give up such outstanding research subjects.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: You were in the right place at the right time. Helping the "Razor" Squad has absolved you of some of your guilt. This order wouldn't have been made otherwise.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Then, may I consider myself reconciled with the Foundation, Madam Lindsay?

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: Of course.

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: Oh, this is wonderful, little musical note! You've got your friends back!

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: I have all kinds of friends, too. Even now, they're all around me!

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: But I'm very sorry. I know you're trying to help me, but I can't go to the Foundation.

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: There are still things I must do. Right, Mama and Papa?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Don't worry, Lorelei.
Semmelweis pulls an item out of Lorelei's pocket.

items.speaker: Razor
items.text: What ...?! What's that doing here?!

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: So this IS the treasure you were looking for?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: "Razor," I offer you a trade.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I'll give you this.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But in return, "Razor" Squad must give asylum to the members of my Field Agent Squad and as many civilians as possible.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: What an unwise decision. If you hand that over to the Foundation without fuss, all your previous wrongdoings will be forgiven.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: When did you become so soft?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: ... I never really cared about these people.

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: But you do now, right? Well done, my dear. You must've realized what a joy it is to help others!

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: No. I'm afraid I've never found an ounce of pleasure in helping anyone.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I'm just a selfish person.

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: But you ARE helping them! You shouldn't put yourself down like that.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I'm only helping them because that's what you want.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: To me, they're just pawns—to ensure I get you.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: If you don't come to the Foundation with me, I'll change my mind and leave these people to fend for themselves.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: And, yes, that's a threat.

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: Oh, so that's your plan!
Lorelei tilts her head, thinking carefully.

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: Mama, Papa, what do you think I should do?
She looks off into the empty space before her, earnestly asking for her hallucinations' advice.

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: But if I leave here with the little musical note, I'll never see you again.

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: The "Flood" will wash away all traces of our lives, and the world I face will be totally different.

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: Hmm, I suppose that makes sense ...

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: But Mama's right. You'll always be with me in my hallucinations.

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: If that's the case, I shouldn't stay in this valley, right?
Lorelei's question isn't directed at her hallucinations but at the silent Semmelweis beside her.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Right. Only by surviving will you have the chance to see a more beautiful and memorable valley, Lorelei.

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: Alright. I'll go with you, my dear!

items.speaker: Lorelei
items.text: Goodbye, Mama! Goodbye, Papa!
Thanks to Lorelei's arcane skill, the previously crazed members of the "Razor" Squad are calmed. They fall into a deep sleep.
A familiar voice echoes from the communication device.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: Semmelweis, do you have a moment to talk?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Of course, Madam Lindsay.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: I'm sorry for lying to you about Laplace.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: But I have no regrets. As a member of the Foundation, I must do everything I can to preserve its strength.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I understand your motives, Madam Lindsay.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: You hid the truth of the situation from me, just as I hid my true intentions from you.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: In that regard, we're even.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: In any case, I should congratulate you for surviving.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: As my superior?

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: No, on a personal level. As a member of the Foundation, I have no comment on the matter.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: I also want to congratulate you on saving that little girl and those humans ... That wasn't like you.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: People change all the time, Madam Lindsay.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Honestly, when Lorelei made the decision, I was relieved.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I really had no clue which way she would go ... Ha, you never can know what an arcanist lunatic is thinking.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: You're not much different.

items.speaker: Madam Lindsay
items.text: Oh, and I suppose one last round of congratulations is in order. You are now a true arcanist—an arcanist I cannot understand.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Thank you.
THE END
